jobs.prompt:
fix(cpp): repair the fuzz link and one delivery test after the memory telemetry change

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-memory-2-20261121-44963979665-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`), C++ only (do NOT install or run Bun, Node, Deno, Rust or Cargo). The branch adds process and cache memory reporting (`include/uos/rt/memory.hpp` and its implementation; report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-memory-2-20261121.md`) and memory fixes. Its hosted CI (`.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-ci.yml`) fails in two ways. Read `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test>`) and `cpp/gateway/fuzz/ci.py`. Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body (three short paragraphs).

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner, Ubuntu 26.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network. `sudo apt-get install -y clang ninja-build pkg-config ccache libboost-json-dev libboost-container-dev libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev zlib1g-dev libicu-dev libbrotli-dev libzstd-dev`; the CI workflow shows the exact list and how it builds the pinned SQLite.

RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Local mocks only.
- Your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed: commit after each fix. No foreground command longer than about 10 minutes.
- Do not delete or weaken tests.

TASK
1. All 25 "robustness (...)" jobs fail at link time, for example: `json_simdjson.hpp:41: undefined reference to 'uos::rt::memory::bytes(...)'` and `memory.hpp:52: undefined reference to 'uos::rt::memory::ScopedCache::set(unsigned long, unsigned long)'`. The fuzz builds (`cpp/gateway/fuzz/targets.json`, `fuzz/ci.py`, and any other source list: `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `tools/links.py` data, `cmake/**`, packaging lists) do not include the new memory implementation source that every user of `src/rt/json_simdjson.hpp` now needs. Add it wherever the runtime sources are listed so EVERY consumer links, then prove it by building every fuzz target the workflow discovers with the workflow's own commands (build, then run each for 10 seconds), one at a time.
2. `tests/serve_delivery_http_test.cpp`, case "provider read failure persists client failure evidence once and preserves the downstream error" (line ~337), fails in release and sanitizer builds: the terminal log now carries the new memory fields and the test compares the whole normalised log to a fixed expected object. Make the comparison correct: normalise the memory fields the way the test already normalises other volatile fields (they are process measurements, so assert that they are present and are non-negative integers, then exclude their values from the exact comparison). Do not drop any other field from the comparison. Search the test tree for other exact terminal-log comparisons that need the same treatment and fix them the same way.
3. Run `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`, the tests linking the files you changed in release and `--config asan`, and release shard 2 (`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard 2/4`) in the background.

DONE WHEN
Every fuzz target builds and runs, shard 2 passes in release, the changed tests pass under sanitizers, and the links check passes.
